content.instructions: To perform a calculation, enter the required variables. Once all the inputs are entered, click the "Calculate" button to perform the calculation. Any time an input variable is adjusted, the "Calculate" button must be clicked to populate the new output. To start over, click the "Reset" button to clear all values and begin the calculation again. Equianalgesic doses are only approximations and substantial interpatient variability exists, including incomplete cross-tolerance when switching between opioids. An empiric 25% to 50% reduction of the calculated equianalgesic dose of the new opioid is recommended to reduce the risk of adverse effects and unintentional overdose. Dose reductions closer to the upper end of this range (ie, 50%) may be appropriate in patients on relatively high opioid doses, or with advanced age or reduced end-organ function (eg, kidney or liver dysfunction); dose reductions closer to the lower end of this range (ie, 25%) may be appropriate in patients on relatively low opioid doses (Fine 2009). Equianalgesic ratios may change according to the direction of the switch; the risk of negative consequences associated with this difference may increase as opioid dosage increases (Anderson 2001; Pereira 2001; Treillet 2018). Other patient-specific factors, such as duration of opioid therapy, genetic polymorphisms, concomitant medications, and presence of hyperalgesia must also be considered. Additionally, the elimination half-life of the opioid must be accounted for, as clinical changes associated with switching from an opioid with a long be accounted for, as clinical changes associated with switching from an opioid with a long half-life may be delayed. Following conversion, monitor closely and adjust dosage if needed to achieve patient-centered goals; breakthrough pain relief with immediate-release opioid formulations may be required (Fine 2009; Knotkova 2009; Pereira 2001; Treillet 2018). general: The drug selections for “Of” and “To” cannot be the same

To use the calculator, determine the total daily dose of the opioid to convert from, enter this dose in the “Convert from” text box, and select this opioid name/route in the “Of” drop-down menu. Then, select the opioid to convert to in the “To” drop-down menu and click “Calculate” to determine the approximate equianalgesic daily dose of the new opioid.
